title: Protect the position before extending the line.
dek: In Chapter 13 of Positioning, Al Ries and Jack Trout explain the conditions under which line extension can work without dissolving the mental position a brand has earned.

marginNote.label: Apprenticeship Note
marginNote.body: Growth does not automatically justify a broader name. Before extending a line, test whether the new offer strengthens the position people already hold or asks the name to mean two conflicting things.

canon.heading: Extend the line only when the position survives the extension.
canon.standfirst: Read the opening section of Chapter 13, "When Line Extension Can Work," from Al Ries and Jack Trout's Positioning on PDF pages 207-226. Study the exceptions and conditions that keep a broader offer from weakening the association already held in the mind, then stop at PDF page 226.
canon.readerIntro: Read this section as a study of mental clarity under growth pressure. Mark the circumstances in which a new product can borrow a name without confusing its position, the dangers that make line extension attractive but weak, and the difference between short-term distribution and long-term memory. Then audit one proposed extension: name the existing position, the new category, and the condition that would make the extension strengthen rather than blur the brand. Stop at PDF page 226.

blocks.label: 01 / Start with the position in the mind
paragraphs: A line extension is not only a product decision; it is a meaning decision. Begin by naming what the existing brand already stands for before asking whether the same name can travel.
Notice which associations are strong enough to be protected and which are too vague to guide a new offer.

blocks.label: 02 / Study when the exception works
paragraphs: The chapter does not treat every extension as identical. Study the conditions that can make an extension credible, especially category expectations, naming clarity, and whether the original position remains legible.
Separate a useful transfer of memory from a name being stretched simply because it is familiar.

blocks.label: 03 / Test the cost of borrowed meaning
paragraphs: An extension may create immediate availability while weakening the association that made the original brand valuable. Track both effects instead of treating launch response as proof of strategic fit.
Ask what the customer would remember after seeing the two offers together and whether that memory helps or hinders the intended choice.

blocks.label: 04 / Audit one proposed extension
paragraphs: Choose one real or hypothetical extension. Write the current position, the new category, the customer expectation, and the condition under which the shared name would clarify rather than confuse.
Finish with a decision: extend, use a separate name, or narrow the offer until the position is once again easy to hold in one sentence.

closeReading: What specific condition allows a line extension to work without dissolving the original position?
Which short-term advantage makes line extension tempting, and what long-term mental cost does the chapter set against it?
How does the customer’s category expectation affect whether the shared name clarifies or confuses the offer?
Choose one brand extension: what does the original name stand for, and what would the customer remember after seeing both offers?
Rewrite one extension proposal so its category, promise, and naming relationship are clear in a single sentence.

principle.heading: Earn the extension by protecting the association.
principle.body: A broader offer is strategically useful only when the shared name makes the desired category easier to recognize rather than asking one mental slot to carry conflicting meanings.
principle.example: Before putting a trusted specialist name on a mass-market product, ask whether the new product reinforces the specialist association or quietly replaces it with a broader, weaker promise.
principle.practice: Pick one proposed line extension. Write the existing position, the new category, the immediate business benefit, and the possible memory cost. Decide whether the shared name strengthens the position, then state the condition that would have to be true for you to proceed.

output.heading: Make growth clarify the name.
output.body: Extend a line only when the new offer makes the brand's position easier to remember, easier to choose, and harder to confuse.

signals.heading: Five current signals on protecting a clear position while offers, channels, and capabilities expand.

fieldNotes.title: OpenAI moves its engineering proof from chat into physical products
fieldNotes.whatHappened: OpenAI described workflows in which its models help engineers design, simulate, and build physical products, including a test device designed with Astra, and said internal hardware-team model usage has grown 23-fold since February.
fieldNotes.whyItMatters: The expansion is credible when the new capability strengthens the core promise—faster, more integrated engineering iteration—instead of asking the same name to stand for unrelated automation. The proof is the workflow and the review loop, not the breadth of the feature list.
fieldNotes.watch: Watch whether production constraints, human review, and measurable iteration gains keep the capability anchored to engineering rather than turning it into a vague general-purpose promise.

fieldNotes.title: Svedka turns AI backlash into a consumer-made Super Bowl brief
fieldNotes.whatHappened: After criticism of its AI-produced 2026 Super Bowl ad, Svedka invited consumers to create a 15-second ad for its ready-to-drink Vodka Water, offering a $500,000 prize and a submission toolkit.
fieldNotes.whyItMatters: The brand is extending into participation while keeping the product and the original criticism as the frame. The move works only if the audience's contribution makes the brand's position more vivid, rather than replacing a clear association with a generic contest mechanic.
fieldNotes.watch: Watch whether the winning work creates distinctive memory for Svedka's product or merely produces a large volume of attention around the act of entering.

fieldNotes.title: Retail Dive says AI recommendations are sending more shoppers into returns
fieldNotes.whatHappened: Retail Dive reported that AI recommendations are contributing to returns and pointed to product-description data as a likely part of the problem.
fieldNotes.whyItMatters: A shopping assistant can extend a retailer's position only when its recommendation makes the product easier to understand and choose. If weak catalog data creates the wrong expectation, the new layer borrows trust from the retailer while weakening the underlying promise.
fieldNotes.watch: Watch whether retailers improve structured product facts, fit and compatibility details, and post-purchase feedback before expanding recommendation surfaces.

fieldNotes.title: TechCrunch puts distribution ahead of technology at its founder summit
fieldNotes.whatHappened: TechCrunch's Nov. 4 Founder Summit agenda foregrounds a session titled "The Next Startup Advantage: Distribution Beats Technology," alongside discussions of AI-enabled small teams and the difficulty of getting customers to discover, adopt, and pay for products.
fieldNotes.whyItMatters: The framing is a useful guardrail against capability-led line extension: a new feature earns a position only when a clear distribution path makes the product discoverable and adoptable. More technology does not automatically create a stronger mental category.
fieldNotes.watch: Watch which AI-native products pair a distinctive promise with a repeatable route to customers, rather than treating launch velocity as evidence that the market has assigned them a position.

fieldNotes.title: Levi's puts sweaters at the center of a jeans brand's holiday story
fieldNotes.whatHappened: Levi's holiday campaign makes sweaters the hero while retaining a craft-led visual language through a claymation yeti, Gus, and a reference to the brand's 1995 claymation spot.
fieldNotes.whyItMatters: This is a controlled line extension: the product broadens, but the tactile craft cue and recognizable brand world carry the original association into the new category. The new offer earns attention by making the old position visible again.
fieldNotes.watch: Watch whether the campaign makes Levi's credible in sweaters beyond the holiday story, and whether the craft association transfers to product consideration rather than stopping at entertainment.

tweets.author: Gergely Orosz
tweets.title: A startup wins when the new physics force a new story
tweets.summary: This is worth keeping because it treats narrative as part of the operating system, not decoration. A strange technical or market bet has to become desirable before incumbents copy it, and the company has to keep moving fast enough that the story remains attached to real progress.
tweets.text: From a startup founder: “it’s now a red flag for me if I don’t see side projects on someone’s resume / application, because it signals lack of autonomy. Because it’s now so trivial to build anything on the side, vs before.”
